Gazprom PJSC Posts Steady Revenue Growth Amid Stable Demand

Gazprom PJSC reported a 6.2% year-on-year rise in quarterly revenue, reflecting resilient domestic demand and moderate gains in key export markets, according to financial results released Tuesday. The Russian oil and gas producer posted revenues of RUB 2.13 trillion for the quarter, compared to RUB 2.01 trillion during the same period last year. Net profit rose 3.8% to RUB 307 billion.

Company executives attributed the uptick to steady flows through major pipeline corridors and sustained consumption in Europe and Central Asia, despite challenging market conditions. “Our focus on reliable supply and operational efficiency continues to support our financial performance,” said Elena Smirnova, Gazprom PJSC’s Chief Financial Officer, during an investor call. She noted that the company had maintained investments in infrastructure projects, including the expansion of the Volga Transmission Line, to secure future growth.

Exports to Western Europe remained stable, while shipments to emerging markets in Asia edged higher, offsetting minor declines in smaller regions. Industry analysts described the results as broadly in line with market expectations. “Gazprom has shown a disciplined approach to capital expenditure and has managed to sustain profitability despite fluctuating commodity prices,” said Yuri Antonov, senior analyst at Eastern Markets Research.

Operating costs rose 4.1% year-on-year, primarily due to increased maintenance spending and wage adjustments agreed earlier this year with the national oil and gas union. The company’s board recommended an interim dividend of RUB 7.50 per share, unchanged from the previous quarter.

The Russian Association of Oil and Gas Producers welcomed the results, citing Gazprom PJSC’s contribution to sector stability and energy security. “These results demonstrate the robustness of Russia’s energy sector and its key players,” said association president Viktor Lebedev.

Gazprom PJSC’s shares closed up 1.3% on the Moscow Exchange following the earnings release.
